title: fix(app-shell): Studio's field inspector offers no Default value control on a record, location or address field (objectui#11947)
body:
Fixes #11947

Clause-②: no

## What changed

`ObjectFieldInspector`'s `defaultValueKind` puts `record`, `location` and `address` on its `noDefault` list, beside `composite` and `repeater`. Studio's field inspector now renders no *Default value* control for these three types. Every other type renders the control it rendered before.

Files: `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ObjectFieldInspector.tsx` (the list and its doc comment), the new pin `ObjectFieldInspector.recordNoDefault-11947.test.tsx` beside it, and `.changeset/11947-record-no-default.md` (patch, `@object-ui/app-shell`).

## Why

A `record` field stores a record. `FieldSchema` checks a literal default against the field's own stored value contract. The inspector showed a text box for a `record` default, so committing `primary` wrote `{ type: 'record', label: 'F', defaultValue: 'primary' }`, and the spec refused it: "the default \"primary\" cannot satisfy this field's own stored value contract — Invalid input: expected record, received string". No control in the inspector can write a record. So `record` joins the no-default list, as the triage comment `6057493875` directs. A structured default editor is not part of this change.

### Fixed here too: `location` and `address` (same defect, same fix)

I checked every type in the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0 `FieldSchema` vocabulary that gets the text control, with `defaultValue: 'primary'`. `location` and `address` store an object, and the spec refuses the string the same way: "expected object, received string". Both are in Studio's palette today. The showcase's `showcase_field_zoo` declares both, as `f_location` and `f_address`.

They are fixed here under the bounded in-place exemption, because all four of its conditions hold:
- It is the same defect class.
- It is the same mechanical one-word fix triage chose for `record`.
- No other claim holds this file.
- It uses the same gate family.

The claim's file surface names only `record`, so I am asking the seat to add these two types to it.

## Measurements (the dispatch's hypotheses)

- **H1 holds.** Measured through the real inspector, the showcase-shaped `{ type: 'record', label: 'F' }` renders 0 default controls after the fix. Before the fix it rendered 1, as the ablation below shows. Control: `text` renders 1 control, and the value it commits parses through `FieldSchema`. Control: `composite` renders 0.
- **H2: a default stored in code.**
  - Before the fix, the text box showed a stored record as `[object Object]`. That control commits the box's text as the default on every keystroke.
  - An unrelated edit (ticking Required) kept the stored record both before and after the fix. That pin is green on both sides of the ablation.
  - After the fix, nothing renders the record as text.
- **H3 holds.** `defaultValueKind` is not exported. Its only callers are the two reads at the *Default value* render site in the same file. `git grep defaultValueKind` finds 3 hits: the definition and those two reads.

## Tests and gates

All of these ran at HEAD `b9ff4fb92`.

- **Ablation.** The fix was committed before the mutation. `ablation-replace.mjs` removed the three entries from the list: anchor count x1 to x0, blob `d5e7618af95d` to `a2e2d2eee2fc`.
  - Result: `Tests 4 failed | 4 passed (8)`. The three no-control pins went red, and so did the "nothing shows the stored record as text" pin. The text and composite controls stayed green, as did the refusal pin and the unrelated-edit pin. I expected red, and it went red.
  - Restore: the blob equals HEAD (`d5e7618af95d`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- **Repo-root `pnpm exec vitest run`.** It covered the new file, every test importing `ObjectFieldInspector` (18 files, objectui#11793's type-picker pin among them) and `column-identity.ratchet.test.ts`: `Test Files 20 passed (20)`, `Tests 311 passed (311)`.
- **Type-check.** `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/app-shell^...` reported `Tasks: 28 successful, 28 total`. Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` passed (`TYPECHECK-OK`, lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`). The test tsconfig lists the new file: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` gives 1 hit.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0. `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: exit 0. `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `0 new citation(s)`, exit 0. `pnpm check:control-bytes`: exit 0.
- These gates also read the touched paths, and each exited 0: `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:designer-field-key-parity`, `check:i18n-keys` and `check:metadata-write-doors`.
- **ESLint** on the two touched source files: exit 0, 0 errors across 2 files (counted from `--format json`). The 11 warnings are all existing `no-explicit-any` hits on lines this change does not touch.
- **Eager closure: NOT MEASURED locally.** The CI budget bot reads it.

## Acceptance notes

- `rating`, `slider` and `progress` also get the text control, but they store a number, so the spec refuses the string it writes: "expected number, received string". They are not fixed here. The right fix is probably a number control rather than no control, and no ruling has made that choice. I have reported this to the seat.
- `date`, `datetime` and `time` refuse a malformed string, but they accept a well-formed one, and the text control can write that. That is a value check, not this shape defect.
- plugin-designer's `FieldDesigner` turns every default value into a string. Its host, `MetadataFieldsPage`, is exported but not mounted in the console, so I did not measure whether anyone can reach it. Noted only.
- Docs: no page under `content/docs` describes the inspector's per-type default control, and neither does the package README. There is nothing to update.
